Additional scope changes accepted without timeline adjustment
Post-MVP feature set finalized without corresponding schedule buffer

potentialImpact.schedule: High likelihood of missing December 31, 2026 contract end date for full delivery; compressed final sprints may force deferral of lower-priority features or incomplete integration testing
potentialImpact.cost: Potential budget pressure from inefficient rework and extended effort on scope changes; risk of exceeding $1,772,253 not-to-exceed threshold if extension discussions arise
potentialImpact.quality: Rushed delivery in final weeks may reduce testing coverage, increase defect escape rate, and compromise production readiness
potentialImpact.customer: Client confidence erosion if committed AI transformation outcomes are not fully realized; potential escalation and governance friction
potentialImpact.operations: Incomplete operational readiness documentation, runbooks, and knowledge transfer may impair post-go-live support and sustainability

supportingHistoricalPatterns: Producer Portal absorbed 14 scope changes equivalent to 0.75-1 sprint without timeline protection, threatening delivery

predictedRisks.reasoning: The risk is highly likely because MVP scope has been unfrozen since at least June 22, 2026 with no resolution, and the project exhibits active scope instability through mid-sprint PBI additions and 4 spilled items in the current sprint. Historical evidence from the same client shows scope creep absorbed significant effort without timeline adjustment, and current declining velocity (merge rate dropping from 16 to 11 over 3 sprints) reduces remaining capacity. With 43.3% of contract time left and substantial work including unresolved architecture decisions, post-MVP features, and production stabilization, the compressed timeline creates high schedule overrun risk relevant to the current build phase and critical for upcoming release phases.
